newsitem.title: CHINA: China frees Hong Kong journalist Xi Yang.
newsitem.headline: China frees Hong Kong journalist Xi Yang.

text.p: China on Saturday released on parole Hong Kong journalist Xi Yang, who had been serving a 12-year prison term for stealing state secrets, the official Xinhua news agency said.
Xi, a former reporter for Hong Kong's Chinese-language Ming Pao newspaper, was released with 157 days to go before the British colony reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997.
He left Beijing for Hong Kong on Saturday evening, Xinhua said.
Xi was paroled because he "showed signs of repentance", the agency said.

China jailed Xi for 12 years in 1994 for stealing state secrets about internal policies on interest rates and gold. The severity of the sentence shocked Hong Kong reporters, already pessimistic about the prospects for a free press after the handover and triggered protests in the British colony.
